intro.text: FTAI Aviation Ltd. (Nasdaq: FTAI) is a Cayman Islands exempted company. Except as otherwise specified, “we”, “us”, “our”, “FTAI”, “FTAI Aviation” or “the Company” refer to us and our consolidated subsidiaries. We are a leading independent engine maintenance platform focused on the CFM56-5B, CFM56-7B and V2500 aircraft engines which power the 737NG and A320ceo aircraft. We repair and rebuild engines in our maintenance facilities and with our joint venture partners, and sell or lease the engines to airlines and asset owners around the world. Our primary business model is to sell or lease engines via exchange through our proprietary Maintenance, Repair and Exchange (“MRE”) model which is reported under our Aerospace Products segment.

s.t: As of December 31, 2025, the Company invested $ 291.5 million in the 2025 Partnership.

During the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company invested $ 20.0 million in the 2026 Partnership.

On June 5, 2025, the Company invested $ 10.5 million for a 50 % interest in Quick Turn Engine Center Europe S.r.l. (previously IAG Engine Center Europe S.r.l.) or “QuickTurn Europe”, a 200,000 square-foot CFM56 engine maintenance repair and overhaul facility located at the Rome Fiumicino Airport.
During the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company invested $ 2.5 million for a 49 % interest in J&F Power Systems LLC ("J&F"), the Company's joint venture with Jereh Group.

As of September 30, 2026, we held an approximately 19% and 21% capital interest in the 2025 Partnership and 2026 Partnership, respectively, with a carrying value of $341.2 million and $12.9 million, respectively.
During 2026, we invested in J&F Power Systems LLC (“J&F”), the Company’s joint venture with Jereh Group.
The 2025 Partnership is an investment focused on acquiring 737NG and A320ceo on-lease narrowbody aircraft, for which the Company is the Servicer and holds a 19 % limited partner ownership.

The Company's proportionate share of equity in earnings related to this investment is based on the contractual profit-sharing arrangement and the elimination of profit on sales of engine and modules to the 2025 Partnership under ASC 606.
